provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Farming in my area
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name crops grown in their area.
The pupils should be able to list at least three crops.

Introduction:
We have seen plants in our school garden.
Today we will talk about crops we grow in our area.

Content:
Crops are plants we grow for food.
In Nigeria we grow maize, yam and cassava.
Maize is like our corn on the cob.
Yam is a big root like sweet potato.
Cassava is used to make garri.

Class activity:
Let us play a game.
I will show pictures of crops.
You will call out the names.

Evaluation questions:
Name one crop grown in Nigeria.
What do we use yam for?
List three crops.

Summary:
Many crops grow in our area for food.

topics.title: Tools of the farmer
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify farming tools.
The pupils should be able to state the uses of hoe and cutlass.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about crops.
Farmers use tools to help them grow crops.

Content:
A hoe is a farming tool with a flat blade.
We use hoe to dig the soil.
A cutlass has a long sharp blade.
We use cutlass to cut plants and weeds.
Farmers carry these tools to their farms.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to be farmers.
Show me how you use a hoe.
Show me how you use a cutlass.

Evaluation questions:
What is a hoe used for?
Name one farming tool.
How do farmers carry tools?

Summary:
Farmers use tools like hoe and cutlass.

topics.title: Planting a small garden
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to prepare a garden bed.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate planting seeds.

Introduction:\We have seen farming tools.
Today we will learn how to plant a small garden.

Content:
First prepare the garden bed.
Clear the grass and dig the soil.
Make small holes in the soil.
Put one seed in each hole.
Cover the seeds with soil.
Water the seeds every day.

Class activity:
Let us plant bean seeds in small cups.
Each pupil will put one seed in soil.
We will water them and watch them grow.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do first to prepare a bed?
How many seeds go in one hole?
What do plants need to grow?

Summary:
We can plant seeds in soil and water them.

topics.title: Weeding the garden
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify weeds in a garden.
The pupils should be able to explain how to care for plants.

Introduction:
Last week we planted seeds in our garden.
Today we will learn how to take care of them.

Content:
Weeds are unwanted plants in the garden.
Weeds take food and water from our crops.
We must remove weeds by pulling them out.
We must water our plants every day.
Plants need sun to grow well.

Class activity:
Let us go to the school garden.
Each pupil will pull one weed.
We will water the plants together.

Evaluation questions:
What are weeds?
Why do we remove weeds?
How do we care for plants?

Summary:
We must remove weeds and water plants.

topics.title: Harvesting
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to harvest crops.
The pupils should be able to state how to store harvested crops.

Introduction:
Our plants have grown big and strong.
It is time to harvest them and store them.

Content:
Harvesting means picking crops when they are ready.
We dig up root crops like yam and cassava.
We pick fruit crops like maize and tomatoes.
After harvesting we must store crops well.
We can keep crops in a cool dry place.
Some crops we can dry in the sun.

Class activity:
Let us pretend to harvest maize.
Each pupil will pick one maize from the plant.
We will put them in a basket.

Evaluation questions:
What does harvesting mean?
Name one root crop we harvest.
How do we store crops?

Summary:
We harvest crops when they are ready.

topics.title: Fish farming basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify fish in ponds.
The pupils should be able to talk about fish farming.

Introduction:
We have learned about crops on land.
Today we will learn about fish in water.

Content:
Fish are animals that live in water.
Fish farming is growing fish in ponds.
Farmers put fish fingerlings in ponds.
The fish eat small plants and insects.
After some time the fish grow big.
We can catch the fish for food.

Class activity:
Let us draw a fish pond.
Each pupil will draw fish in water.
We will color our drawings.

Evaluation questions:
Where do fish live?
What do fish eat?
What is fish farming?

Summary:
Fish are grown in ponds for food.

topics.title: Selling and buying
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate simple buying and selling.
The pupils should be able to count change correctly.

Introduction:
We have learned about farming and harvesting.
Today we will learn how to sell what we grow.

Content:
When we sell things we give them to people for money.
When we buy things we give money to get things.
We use naira to buy things in Nigeria.
We must count money carefully.
If something costs 10 naira and you give 20 naira.
You should get 10 naira as change.

Class activity:
Let us play a market game.
Some pupils will be sellers.
Some pupils will be buyers.
Use toy money to buy fruits.

Evaluation questions:
What do we use to buy things?
If you buy something for 5 naira and give 10 naira what change do you get?
What is selling?

Summary:
We buy and sell things using money.

topics.title: Making simple snacks
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to wash fruits properly.
The pupils should be able to prepare a simple fruit plate.

Introduction:
We have learned about selling crops.
Today we will learn to make simple snacks from fruits.

Content:
First we wash our hands with soap.
Then we wash fruits with clean water.
We peel fruits like banana and orange.
We cut fruits into small pieces.
We arrange fruits on a plate nicely.
We can share our fruit plate with friends.

Class activity:
Let us prepare a fruit salad.
Each pupil will wash one fruit.
We will cut and arrange fruits together.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do first before preparing fruits?
Name one fruit we can use for snack.
How do we arrange fruits?

Summary:
We can wash and prepare fruits for snacks.

topics.title: Safety with tools
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to carry tools safely.
The pupils should be able to state where to keep tools when not in use.

Introduction:
We have learned about farming tools.
Today we will learn how to use tools safely.

Content:
Tools can be dangerous if not used well.
When carrying tools we must point them down.
We must not run with tools in our hands.
When we finish using tools we keep them away.
Tools should be kept in a safe place.
Children should not use tools alone.

Class activity:
Let us practice carrying tools safely.
Each pupil will pick up a toy hoe.
Walk slowly and point it down.

Evaluation questions:
How should we carry tools?
Where do we keep tools when not using them?
Why is safety important with tools?

Summary:
We must be careful when using tools.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what they learned this year.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about farming.

Introduction:
This is the last week of school.
We will revise what we learned this year.

Content:
We learned about crops we grow in our area.
We learned about farming tools like hoe and cutlass.
We learned how to plant and care for plants.
We learned about harvesting and storing crops.
We learned about fish farming.
We learned about buying and selling.
We learned to make simple snacks.
We learned to use tools safely.

Class activity:
Let us play a quiz game.
I will ask questions about what we learned.
Raise your hand to answer.

Evaluation questions:
Name two crops grown in Nigeria.
What tool do farmers use to dig soil?
How do we care for plants?
What do fish eat?
How do we keep tools safe?

Summary:
We have learned many things about farming this year.
